sentences.text: Federal reports addressed violence against women and its relationship to women's status, with the Standing Committee on Health and Welfare, Social Affairs, Seniors and the Status of Women issuing a report titled "The War Against Women" that exposed the issue of violence against women and drew links between violence and the need to alter the status of women and traditional behaviours that structure gender relations.
Federal government initiatives focused on prevention and education, the justice system, and services for victims, offenders and their families in response to the violence against women issue.

Federal reports indicated that statistics on women's economic equality, adequate childcare, and equal access to training and post-secondary education remained unchanged despite twenty years of promised improvements.

Status of Women Canada worked on developing economic models to calculate women's loss of earning capacity when assuming family responsibilities and to assist in calculating spousal support in divorce cases.
Federal reports noted that strategies were being promoted to increase the participation of girls and women in mathematics, science and technology to help women prepare for a restructured economy.
